note: Story director on the new core (docs/design/director-on-core2.md). Developer data, never shown to a player. Channels, kept-fact kinds and tie rows are open data rows; the code registers one measure per channel operation.

directorMomentFloor.citation: Owner answer 1, October 9, 2026: the smallest adult row of the Holmes and Rahe Social Readjustment Rating Scale, 'Minor violations of the law', 11 life-change units divided by 100. Holmes, T. H., and Rahe, R. H. (1967), Journal of Psychosomatic Research 11(2):213-218.
directorMomentFloor.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967) Social Readjustment Rating Scale

directorInterruptImpact.citation: Owner ruling on answer 2, October 9, 2026: the scale's anchor event, 'Marriage', 50 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), so losing a household's only pay takes over the screen.

directorScaleFeeling.citation: Identity: the core's appraised event impulses are already expressed on the life-change scale divided by 100 (src/core2/emotion.ts appraiseEvent).

directorFeelingSignals.citation: The core's appraisal carries an event's size on two signals, mood and stress (src/core2/emotion.ts appraiseEvent); the drives package puts the same life-change share on each (src/core2/modules/health.ts severityImpulse). Averaging the two returns that share.

directorScaleTie.citation: Holmes and Rahe (1967) 'Change in number of arguments with spouse', 35 life-change units divided by 100; the October 8, 2026 story director design caps relationship moments at this row.
directorScaleTie.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967) Social Readjustment Rating Scale

directorScaleCause.citation: Identity: drive strength from the drives package is already trait-weighted on the life-change impulse scale.

directorScaleReentry.citation: Identity: a re-entry adds the pair's importance from before it faded, which is already a sum of moment impacts and standing ties (October 8, 2026 story director design, part 5, rule 1).

directorScaleMoney.citation: Holmes and Rahe (1967) 'Fired at work', 47 life-change units divided by 100, applied to a loss of the household's whole yearly pay.
directorScaleMoney.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967) Social Readjustment Rating Scale

directorScaleHome.citation: Holmes and Rahe (1967) 'Change in residence', 20 life-change units divided by 100.
directorScaleHome.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967) Social Readjustment Rating Scale

directorScaleHealth.citation: The watched person's own death ends the watched life; scale 1 places it at the top of the life-change scale. No direct source for the director's weighting.

directorWeightTieSociability.citation: The October 8, 2026 design's trait tilt at full strength (one quarter), reused for sociability on the tie channel. No direct source.

directorWeightMoneyRisk.citation: The October 8, 2026 design's trait tilt at full strength (one quarter), signed so that a person who avoids risk weighs a money loss more. No direct source.

directorCostHorizonDays.citation: Average Gregorian month: 146,097 days per 400 years divided by 4,800 months.

directorTieParent.citation: Story director design, part 2, October 8, 2026 calibration (data/content/story-threads.json).

directorTieChild.citation: Story director design, part 2, October 8, 2026 calibration (data/content/story-threads.json).

directorTieSibling.citation: Story director design, part 2, October 8, 2026 calibration (data/content/story-threads.json).

directorTieGrandparent.citation: Story director design, part 2, October 8, 2026 calibration (data/content/story-threads.json).

directorTieGrandchild.citation: Story director design, part 2, October 8, 2026 calibration (data/content/story-threads.json).

directorTiePartner.citation: Not in the October 8, 2026 calibration, which had no partner row. Set equal to a parent or child; Holmes and Rahe (1967) rank a spouse's death (100) above a close family member's (63), so this is a floor.
directorTiePartner.estimatedFrom: October 8, 2026 parent tie and Holmes and Rahe (1967) ranking

directorTieSharedHome.citation: Story director design, part 2, October 8, 2026 calibration (data/content/story-threads.json).

directorFadingDiscount.citation: Story director design, part 2, October 8, 2026 calibration: fading discounts a pair's moments by up to three quarters.

directorFriendHalfLifeDays.citation: Owner question 4 (P13 design note): about 18 months. Roberts, S. G. B., and Dunbar, R. I. M. (2015), Managing relationship decay: network, gender, and contextual effects, Human Nature 26(4):426-450, found emotional closeness to friends declined without contact over 18 months.

directorKinHalfLifeDays.citation: Owner question 4 (P13 design note): about 36 months, twice the friend half-life, because Roberts and Dunbar (2015) found kin closeness declined markedly less than friends' without contact.

directorRenewedFading.citation: Labeling only: a contact is labeled a renewal when at least half of the pair's closeness had faded, one half-life. Decides no outcome.

directorAnniversaryHalfDays.citation: Owner answer 7, October 9, 2026: a weight highest on the anniversary that falls smoothly over two weeks either side; it halves every 7 days from the date, with no cut-off. No direct source.

directorPastChildBorn.citation: Owner answer 5, October 9, 2026: a recorded past fact scores the stress scale's 'Gain of a new family member' row, 39 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967).
directorPastChildBorn.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967) Social Readjustment Rating Scale
